statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail is 9% in the low band roughly three and a half hours into the Sunday Globex session.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping yields EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. A narrow evidence-based danger window is flagged over 13:00-15:00 UTC, the window containing Monday's US cash open, where an opening-auction imbalance can extend before it retraces. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: NQ extends to a 30,130.50 high and holds 30,112.50 (+0.65%) in a third consecutive higher hour; Tail edges to 9% while WTI slipping to $97.94 eases Stress to 34%
body:
About three and a half hours into the Globex session the NQ price path has extended again. Futures print 30,112.50, up 195.25 points (+0.65%) against the 29,917.25 Friday settle, inside an observed 29,904.50-30,130.50 range, and the Investing.com feed corroborates the same 30,112.50 print. This is the third consecutive hour of higher prints and the index is holding roughly 18 points under its session high, which is the one meaningful Tail amplifier on the board. Against it, the entire excursion still spans only 0.76%, the session low was set below the settle before the recovery, and the book is a thin Sunday one. Holding near an extreme without observed shallow pullbacks or repeated extension after failed retracements is not the persistent no-retracement structure the Tail measure is defined against.

The cash reference remains Friday's NDX close at 29,644.17, up 0.67%, in a mixed tape where the S&P 500 added 0.17% and the Dow shed 0.18%. Internals were split rather than aligned, and the shared Finviz context for this run is only partial - its futures and calendar sections are unavailable - so the usable part is latest-session breadth showing megacaps evenly divided four to four, Technology up 0.84% against Communication Services down 0.74%, and semiconductors positive five to two with Micron up 3.9% and Broadcom up 3.0% against Qualcomm down 5.8%. That is delayed, latest-session context and is not evidence of live price path; what it does argue is dispersion and rotation rather than index-level one-way structure.

The energy impulse that has been holding Stress up is now decaying faster than the rest of the backdrop. WTI has fallen to $97.94, down 2.35%, and Brent to $101.29, down 2.48%, a fourth consecutive session of declines attributed to diplomatic efforts that could restore regional energy flows. That happened despite genuine weekend escalation: Houthi forces launched missile and drone strikes at Riyadh, Trump warned Iran of dire economic and political consequences without a deal, and Tehran threatened sustained retaliation. Oil falling into that news is the clearest available evidence that the market is currently pricing the diplomatic branch, which is why the escalation is carried as Stress and headline risk rather than as an established Tail path.

The rate backdrop is unchanged and still the heaviest standing weight. The FOMC raised rates 25 basis points to 3.75-4.00% on 16 September, its first hike in three years, and signalled more tightening; Kashkari said on Sunday that inflation is too high in all aspects of the economy, not merely in oil, and supported that hike. The 10-year sits at 4.997% as of the 18 September close, a level last seen in 2007, against 4.75% at the 2-year; the latest H.15 observation, dated 17 September, reads 4.67% and 4.94%. VIX closed at 14.81, down 4.08%, a calm reading against that backdrop.

The week's live catalyst set is diplomatic rather than macro. Bessent and Greer met Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng in New York on Sunday on artificial intelligence, tariffs and critical minerals, ahead of a Trump-Xi summit in Washington later in the week; analysts quoted expect limited steps rather than a broad breakthrough. Under the evidence standard applied here an unresolved diplomatic process widens dispersion and raises Stress; it does not establish a Tail path in advance. Monday's own calendar is light - a Goolsbee speech at 10:30 UTC, the Chicago Fed National Activity Index at 12:30 UTC and bill auctions at 15:30 UTC.

Net: Tail 9%, up one point on the continued extension and the session-high hold, which keeps the mapped state at EA_ON and green. Stress eases to 34% as the fourth straight decline in crude takes WTI under $98, partly offset by the verified weekend escalation. Confidence rises to 77% on two live futures feeds agreeing to the tick, verified oil, yield and volatility levels, a verified seven-day calendar and verified weekend reporting, discounted for the absence of live cash-market cross-asset confirmation over the weekend and for a Finviz context that is only partially collected.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available and describe an unbroken low-Tail regime across the Sunday of the weekend halt and into the Globex reopen. Tail held between 4% and 8% in every hour, mapping to EA_ON and green throughout, and rose only in the closing hours as the reopen produced its first live price path. Stress drifted from 25-26% early on 20 September into a 30-35% band as the post-hike rate backdrop and the elevated oil complex accumulated, reaching 35% in the most recent hour. Confidence ranged from 70% to 76%, dipping in the deepest part of the halt when no live price path existed and recovering once futures reopened. Dominant mode was normal in all 24 hours. The present assessment continues that sequence with Tail at 9%.
outlookSummary: The cycle covers the remainder of the Asian session, the European session, the Monday US cash session through the 20:00 UTC close, the CME maintenance halt and the Tuesday Globex reopen. Tail is projected to stay inside the low band in all 24 hours, so the mapped policy state remains EA_ON throughout. The projected peak is 12% in the hour containing the 13:30 UTC US cash open, followed by 11% in the hour after it, which is why the flagged danger window spans 13:00-15:00 UTC; secondary 10% readings fall on the 12:30 UTC Chicago Fed release, the 15:30 UTC bill auctions and the closing hour into 20:00 UTC. The cycle low of 7% falls in the 21:00-22:00 UTC maintenance halt, when no NQ price path exists. Stress is projected between 33% and 37%, held up by a 5.00% 10-year and a Fed that has just resumed hiking, and capped by the fourth consecutive decline in crude. Confidence decays from 77% to 68% across the cycle as the evidence base ages. These are conditional projections: no future price-path structure is treated as already observed, and an upgrade would require observed shallow pullbacks with repeated extension after failed retracements.
